reasons: Deviation classification is correct: Section 5.1 contains only a services standard-of-care and corporate-authority warranty with no conformance warranty for Deliverables/Materials, no warranty period and no stated remedy, and the broad 'AS IS' disclaimer at p0074 covers all Materials — this fails the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with repair, replace, re-perform or refund) and edges toward walk-away.

Redline is actionable and directionally correct: it inserts a 90-day conformance warranty for Deliverables/Materials with a no-malicious-code assurance and an at-IBM's-option re-perform/repair/refund remedy, and adds an 'Except as expressly warranted in Section 5.1' carve-out so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty — exactly the rule's redline guidance.

The failed 'warranty period ≥ 90 days' regex is a false negative: the inserted text expressly states 'for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery'. The 0.46 changed-character ratio on p0074 is explained by the necessary prefatory carve-out; the disclaimer's substance is otherwise preserved.
Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, cites the playbook and correctly identifies 90 days as the fallback while inviting discussion.

Minor, non-blocking nits: the rationale asserts a compliance-with-laws covenant that is not visible in the cited paragraphs, and the new clause 'c.' follows a subsection 'b.' ending in a period, so the list conjunction may need tidying on execution.
